fr:mainmatter.fr:p: I have been stuck on the proof of follow last soundness for the Kleene star case for a few days. To the point of considering guarded recursion.
I don't exactly understand how guarded recursion works, but I suspect it might be the sort of thing that allows some of these proofs to go through or be simplified.
For instance, the sorts of recursive calls to parsers that aren't structurally recursive, but will be decreasing on the inputted strings.

Also, proofs involving Kleene stars that where I would like to assume the inductive hypothesis on the Kleene star after it has been unrolled once. If I wish to prove follow last soundness for the Kleene star of a deterministic regular expression r,
{r}^{*} \And {\mathopen {}\left ({r}^{*} \otimes c \otimes \top \right )\mathclose {}} \vdash \bot
when r \And {\mathopen {}\left (r \otimes c \otimes \top \right )\mathclose {}} \vdash \bot and r \And {\mathopen {}\left (c \otimes \top \right )\mathclose {}} \vdash \bot .

The proof reduceds to unrolling each of the {r}^{*} and then showing {\mathopen {}\left (r \otimes {r}^{*}\right )\mathclose {}} \And {\mathopen {}\left ({\mathopen {}\left (r \otimes {r}^{*}\right )\mathclose {}} \otimes c \otimes \top \right )\mathclose {}} \vdash \bot
However, my only strategy for such a proof involves invoking an inductive hypothesis for the {r}^{*} terms which would currently be circular reasoning. Although, because they are unrolled once, I suspect I may be able to make some sort of guarded argument and make each of these {r}^{*} to instead be \triangleright {r}^{*}. Then this would allow me to use the inductive hypothesis?

After boarding this out with Pranav. It seems like a very simple solution using star continuity would let me inductively use hypotheses as they relate to concatenations of r. Then I can tie these together by inducting on the indices of the iterated tensors as referenced by continuity.
I don't think this approach would ever nicely generalize to the context free case, so I still suspect that guarded recursion is the way to go.
Thus far I have shown the soundness of our notions of nullability and first sets for the encoding of deterministic regular expresssions in Dependent Lambek Calculus.

I've been primarily stuck on the following proof for the soundness of the followlast sets in the case of concatenation of two nonnullable grammars.
Given g and h such that \mathsf {FLast}(g) and \mathsf {First}(h) are disjoint, and c \not \in \mathsf {FLast}(h), want to show that c is also not in \mathsf {FLast}(g \otimes h).
That is, assuming for all c, g \And {\mathopen {}\left (g \otimes c \otimes \top \right )\mathclose {}} \vdash \bot or h \And {\mathopen {}\left (c \otimes \top \right )\mathclose {}} \vdash \bot . Fix c such that h \And {\mathopen {}\left (h \otimes c \otimes \top \right )\mathclose {}} \vdash \bot , and then show g \otimes h \And {\mathopen {}\left (g \otimes h \otimes c \otimes \top \right )\mathclose {}} \vdash \bot .

This isn't super bad to do in the model, where you do some case analysis. In particular, the string that is parsed splits into some w , x : \mathrm {String} with g and h parses, respectively. Likewise, it splits into y , z : \mathrm {String} with a g parse of y and an h \otimes \texttt {"}c\texttt {"} \otimes \top parse of z. All in all, we have
w,x,y,z : \mathrm {String} , w \texttt { ++ } x = y \texttt { ++ } z with some parses g w, h x, g y, and (h \otimes \texttt {"}c\texttt {"} \otimes \top ) z. Then you split into cases checking whether w and y are the same string, if w is a (nontrivial) prefix of y, or if y is a prefix of w. Then each of the cases are straightforward enough but still tedious.

I've been weighing whether or not to do effectively the same proof but in the model by using the axiom g \cong \textstyle \mathchoice {\textstyle \oplus _{{\mathopen {}\left (w : \mathrm {String}\right )\mathclose {}}}}{\textstyle \oplus _{{\mathopen {}\left (w : \mathrm {String}\right )\mathclose {}}}}{\scriptstyle \oplus _{{\mathopen {}\left (w : \mathrm {String}\right )\mathclose {}}}}{\scriptscriptstyle \oplus _{{\mathopen {}\left (w : \mathrm {String}\right )\mathclose {}}}}. g \And \lceil w \rceil It feels as there should be a way to do this at a high level utilizing type-based reasoning, rather than manipulating individual strings.
